speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I hear you have progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties; to begin my evaluation, have you noticed any changes in your handwriting or swallowing difficulties recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS). The combination of progressive gait disturbance requiring a wheelchair, chronic urinary incontinence, and recent speech slurring in a 54-year-old male strongly suggests a motor neuron disease affecting both bulbar and respiratory muscles. Given the rapid progression and functional decline, I recommend immediate admission for respiratory monitoring, non-invasive ventilation assessment, and initiation of riluzole.
